title: A verified corpus bundle
description: Terms for connecting selected corpus bytes to provenance and keeping content checks separate from retrieval and storage.

terms.definition: The selected raw text and metadata payloads together with their manifest. In this synthetic example, two sources share one license payload and one attribution payload.

The record connecting selected corpus content to its source revision, provenance reference, license text and attribution. Matching those claims does not establish that they are true or grant permission.

A complete corpus record with one fixed byte representation, including content IDs, roles, counts, digests and provenance. The verifier rejects different formatting or ordering rather than silently rewriting it.

The SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical manifest. It identifies the record through its provenance and payload digests; supplied payload bytes still need verification. It is not a signature or permission certificate.
A logical name for one payload in the selected corpus record. A source uses that name to refer to content; adapters choose how to retrieve or store it. The name is not a required filename or URL.
The separate raw text source selected outside the raw training source. Its name does not define the final validation or test split, which is constructed later.
